title: Latest woodchip bioreactor sites reducing fertilizer pollution in local waterways by up to 99%
excerpt: High nitrogen levels entering downstream waterways can harm fragile ecosystems. Across the world, excess nutrients commonly trigger algae blooms and fish kills in enclosed waterways near intensive horticulture.
content_html:
High nitrogen levels entering downstream waterways can harm fragile ecosystems. Across the world, excess nutrients commonly trigger algae blooms and fish kills in enclosed waterways near intensive horticulture.

The bioreactors use woodchips to support naturally occurring bacteria that convert excess nitrate in farm drainage into harmless nitrogen gas before water leaves the property. The bacteria do this by using carbon from the woodchips and nitrogen in the water as food sources.

The technology has proven particularly effective in high-intensity horticultural systems located near important environmental assets such as the Solitary Islands Marine Park, where nutrient-rich runoff poses a significant risk to biodiversity and water quality.

The ongoing partnership between North Coast Local Land Services, City of Coffs Harbor and Southern Cross University has seen the development of more effective bioreactors over the past six years.

Research by Southern Cross University has shown that drainage water from some intensive systems can contain nitrate levels many thousands of times higher than water quality guidelines, particularly where fertilizer and irrigation are not well matched to crop demand.

Project leader Professor Christian Sanders, based at Southern Cross University's National Marine Science Center in Coffs Harbor, congratulated graduate researcher Rebecca Woodrow.

"These results were made possible as a result of a lot of dedicated work by Rebecca. She was able to show the effectiveness of the new bioreactor designs, using specialized equipment as part of her PhD studies," Sanders said.

Woodrow's PhD research showed the newly designed systems, which can now be modified to account for farm wastewater volumes, are able to use naturally occurring bacteria that live on the woodchips to convert nitrate pollution into harmless nitrogen gas before it reaches nearby creeks and the ocean.

"By intercepting farm runoff, bioreactors help reduce the amount of nutrient pollution entering our waterways and important marine regions such as the Solitary Islands Marine Park," Sanders said.

"Importantly, we found that the bioreactors removed substantial amounts of nitrate while producing very little nitrous oxide, a potent greenhouse gas. That means they are reducing water pollution without simply shifting the problem into the atmosphere."

Horticulturalists encouraged to strengthen on-farm nutrient management

Ongoing efforts by North Coast Local Land Services include pairing improved irrigation practices with refined bioreactor designs and testing these efficiencies under extreme weather conditions, promoting their future uptake across the region.

Local Land Services Senior Officer Shaun Morris said the results confirm bioreactors are an important tool and work best when supported by effective input management across the farm.

"North Coast LLS, Southern Cross University and City of Coffs Harbor have clearly shown bioreactors can help treat a range of farm effluents, including nitrate, phosphate and pesticides, before they leave the property," Morris said.

Excess nitrate runoff not only degrades water quality and aquatic ecosystems but can also release nitrous oxide into the atmosphere—a greenhouse gas with a global warming potential around 300 times greater than carbon dioxide.

North Coast Local Land Services General Manager Alison Bowman said climate change and water quality pressures mean horticultural producers need practical, cost-effective solutions that protect both productivity and the environment.

"Climate variability, intense rainfall events and rising environmental risks are already affecting farming on the North Coast," Bowman said. "Bioreactors are a valuable mitigation tool, but long-term protection of waterways relies on improving how nutrients, water and chemicals are managed across the farm."

Optimizing fertilizer use is one of the most effective steps growers can take. Regular soil and tissue testing helps match fertilizer rates to crop needs, reducing excess application and saving input costs. Split fertilizer applications timed to crop growth can further improve nutrient uptake and reduce losses.

"Real progress comes from collaboration. When growers, researchers and industry work together, we see solutions that are practical, effective and scalable," Morris said.

Sanders praised Local Land Services for its pursuit of more effective bioreactors combined with better farm practices.

"With appropriate design, regular monitoring and adjustments to match farm wastewater volumes, bioreactors can achieve high levels of nitrogen removal and provide a strong safeguard against nutrient pollution entering local waterways," Sanders said. "However, they are most effective when used alongside best-practice fertilizer and irrigation management, rather than as a replacement for reducing nitrogen inputs at the source."

content_html_zh:
进入下游水道的高氮含量会损害脆弱的生态系统。 在世界各地，过量的营养物质通常会在集约化园艺附近的封闭水道中引发藻类大量繁殖和鱼类死亡。

生物反应器使用木片来支持自然产生的细菌，这些细菌在水离开农场之前将农场排水中过量的硝酸盐转化为无害的氮气。 细菌利用木片中的碳和水中的氮作为食物来源来做到这一点。

事实证明，该技术对于位于重要环境资产（例如孤岛海洋公园）附近的高强度园艺系统特别有效，那里营养丰富的径流对生物多样性和水质构成了重大风险。

北海岸地方土地服务部、考夫斯港市和南十字星大学之间持续的合作伙伴关系在过去六年中开发出了更有效的生物反应器。

南十字星大学的研究表明，一些集约化系统的排水中硝酸盐含量可能比水质标准高出数千倍，特别是在化肥和灌溉与作物需求不匹配的情况下。

位于考夫斯港的南十字星大学国家海洋科学中心的项目负责人克里斯蒂安·桑德斯教授向研究生研究员丽贝卡·伍德罗表示祝贺。

“这些结果是丽贝卡大量奉献工作的结果。 作为她博士研究的一部分，她能够使用专用设备展示新生物反应器设计的有效性，”桑德斯说。

伍德罗的博士研究表明，新设计的系统现在可以根据农场废水量进行修改，能够利用生活在木片上的天然细菌，在硝酸盐污染到达附近的小溪和海洋之前将其转化为无害的氮气。

桑德斯说：“通过拦截农田径流，生物反应器有助于减少进入我们水道和孤岛海洋公园等重要海洋区域的营养物污染量。”

“重要的是，我们发现生物反应器去除了大量的硝酸盐，同时产生很少的一氧化二氮（一种强效温室气体）。 这意味着他们正在减少水污染，而不是简单地将问题转移到大气中。”

鼓励园艺师加强农场养分管理

北海岸地方土地服务部门正在进行的努力包括将改进的灌溉实践与精细的生物反应器设计相结合，并在极端天气条件下测试这些效率，以促进其在整个地区的未来应用。

当地土地服务高级官员肖恩·莫里斯表示，结果证实生物反应器是一种重要的工具，并且在整个农场有效的投入管理的支持下效果最佳。

莫里斯说：“北海岸 LLS、南十字星大学和考夫斯港市已经清楚地表明，生物反应器可以帮助在一系列农场废水离开农场之前对其进行处理，包括硝酸盐、磷酸盐和农药。”

过量的硝酸盐径流不仅会降低水质和水生生态系统，还会向大气中释放一氧化二氮，这是一种温室气体，其全球变暖潜力约为二氧化碳的 300 倍。

北海岸地方土地服务总经理艾莉森鲍曼表示，气候变化和水质压力意味着园艺生产者需要实用、经济高效的解决方案来保护生产力和环境。

鲍曼说：“气候变化、强降雨事件和不断上升的环境风险已经影响了北海岸的农业。” “生物反应器是一种有价值的缓解工具，但水道的长期保护依赖于改善整个农场的养分、水和化学品的管理方式。”

优化肥料使用是种植者可以采取的最有效的步骤之一。 定期进行土壤和组织测试有助于将施肥量与作物需求相匹配，减少过量施用并节省投入成本。 根据作物生长时机分次施肥可以进一步提高养分吸收并减少损失。

“真正的进步来自于合作。 当种植者、研究人员和行业共同努力时，我们会看到实用、有效和可扩展的解决方案，”莫里斯说。

桑德斯赞扬当地土地服务部追求更有效的生物反应器和更好的农场实践。

桑德斯说：“通过适当的设计、定期监测和调整以匹配农场废水量，生物反应器可以实现高水平的脱氮，并为防止营养物污染进入当地水道提供强有力的保障。” “然而，当它们与最佳实践肥料和灌溉管理一起使用时，它们才是最有效的，而不是作为从源头减少氮输入的替代品。”
